core_obligations: Closure of a connected set: writing the closure of a connected T as a disjoint union of two relatively closed and open pieces forces a corresponding splitting of T, so T lies in one piece and the closure is connected, which gives assertions (1) and (2) (proof lines 888-892).

Uniqueness through the union of connected subsets: the proof shows that the union of a family of connected subsets with a common point is connected, which is what makes the maximal connected set through a point well defined (proof lines 894-910).

Assertions (3) and (4): the maximal connected subset containing a given point is the unique connected component containing it and it is closed by (2), so the connected subsets are each contained in a unique component and the space is their disjoint union (proof lines 910-917).

The sharpness remark: the author closes by exhibiting a space whose connected components are singletons that are not open, which is why assertion (2) says closed but not necessarily open (proof lines 918-919).
proof_roadmap: 把闭包写成两块相对开闭的并，会诱导出连通集 T 的同样分裂，从而 T 落在一块中，得 (1)(2)。
证明“有公共点的连通集之并连通”，由此定义过一点的极大连通集，得 (3)(4)；最后举出连通分量为单点且不开的空间，说明 (2) 中的“不一定开”。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement collects the basic properties of connected components (author lemma at source lines 874-885, label lemma-connected-components): closures of connected sets are connected, components are closed, every connected subset lies in a unique component, and the space is the disjoint union of its components. The proof (source lines 887-920) proves the closure statement by splitting a putative separation of the closure and pulling it back to the connected set (proof lines 888-892), then uses the standard result that a union of connected sets with a common point is connected to define the maximal connected set through a point (proof lines 894-917), and finishes by exhibiting the counterexample to openness of components (proof lines 918-919). The numbered list is the reference point for the rest of the connectedness section. H2.
